title: Experimentation Platform: A/B Exposure & Safety Controls for Model Versions
creator: Samira Chen
description:
Goal: Ship an A/B testing framework for model versions that lets product and platform teams configure controlled experiments (percent splits, targeting rules, ramp schedules), collect statistically valid metrics, and automatically pause/rollback model versions if defined safety or quality checks fail. This feature will be integrated into the Redwood Console and expose APIs/SDK hooks so engineers can opt into experiments per-route or per-customer.

Scope: MVP for hosted + dedicated deployments. Must support: percent exposure by route, user or customer targeting, shadow traffic capture for offline evaluation, metric definitions (latency, token-error rate, task-specific eval score), statistical test plumbing (two-sided t-test + bootstrap for non-normal distributions), configurable stopping rules and auto-rollback policies, and dashboards with experiment-level telemetry and audit logs.

Out of scope for MVP: fully-managed adaptive multi-armed bandit allocation and cross-customer cohort stitching. Private (on-prem) will receive APIs but advanced automation will be gated to later cycles due to upgrade/validation constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Console: Experiment create form allows selecting baseline and candidate model versions, exposure percent (0.1% - 50%), targeting rules (route tag, customer id regex, header-based targeting), and ramp schedule.
Runtime: Requests routed according to experiment rules with deterministic hashing for reproducible assignment and sticky assignment for session-level consistency.
Shadow traffic: Support duplicating 100% of production requests to a candidate model with no response served to end users; captured outputs stored in experiment bucket for offline eval.
Metrics: System collects and stores per-experiment metrics for latency (p50/p95), token-generation errors, and a user-specified evaluation metric; metrics are queryable in Console and via API.
Statistical checks: Built-in two-sample bootstrap test for metric deltas with configurable p-value threshold and minimum sample size guardrails.

Auto-rollback: Policy engine can auto-pause or rollback candidate model if metric delta exceeds configured thresholds (e.g., +25% p95 latency, -2% task accuracy, p<0.01) and creates an incident log + notification to on-call.
Auditability: All experiment changes, exposure ramps, and automatic actions are recorded in the audit log with who/when/why and linked to the model version and commit hash.
Security: Experiment metadata and shadowed payloads respect data retention and PII filters; security review completed and keys not exported in cleartext in logs.
Docs & SDK: Public docs and SDK examples for creating experiments via REST and JS/Python SDKs; a sample GitHub repo with a simple A/B experiment integration example.
Performance: No significant increase (>5%) to baseline  p50 latency for requests not in active experiments when experiment logic is enabled.
notes: Design trade-off: deterministic hashing + sticky session chosen over per-request random split to avoid exposure flapping in chat-like sessions (DES-604 reference).

Stat testing: We prefer bootstrap + non-parametric checks for evaluation metrics that are typically skewed (generation quality scores). Two-sided tests by default; allow one-sided for specific guardrails.
Ramp schedule: Default ramp is 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% over 24h increments; can be customized per experiment. Manual approval required for >20% exposure by default.

Safety defaults: Auto-rollback triggers start conservative (low false-positive tolerance) but create high-visibility alerts for SRE/ML owners. We will iterate thresholds after initial experiments with partner customers.
Telemetry retention: Experiment metrics retained for 90 days in hot store and archived for 1 year for auditability; long-term storage subject to cost/contracting for enterprise customers.
Integration notes: Requires runtime feature flags for deterministic routing (ENG-3120) and KV-store for sticky assignments. Dashboard work depends on console-telemetry APIs (ENG-2897).
Privacy: For shadow traffic we will apply PII scrubbers and sampling for data exported to ML teams; compliance review scheduled with Security team.
